\paragraph{Differential-pulse voltammetry through the channel.} The same bench
also runs differential-pulse voltammetry: the triangular source is replaced by
a staircase-plus-pulse program at the published assay envelope
(Figure~\ref{fig:electrode-dpv}), with every level quantised to the 14-bit DAC
LSB of \SI{152.6}{\micro\volt} (26.2~codes per \SI{4}{\milli\volt} tread), and
the current sampled \SI{5}{\milli\second} before each edge. Four reporters at
distinct formal potentials produce four resolved differential-current peaks;
simulated apexes land within \SI{2}{\milli\volt} and \SI{1}{\percent} of the
assay-derived targets. Three findings from these runs bound how DPV numbers
must be read:

\begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item \emph{There is no residual charging baseline.} A blank (both bulk
    concentrations zero) produces a differential current below
    \SI{1}{\pico\ampere} at every step: \SI{45}{\milli\second} of a
    \SI{50}{\milli\second} pulse is far beyond the
    \SI{200}{\nano\farad}/\SI{1}{\kilo\ohm} double-layer time constant, so
    \(\Delta I = I(S_2)-I(S_1)\) cancels charging entirely at this timing.
  \item \emph{The \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm} tap slew-limits on every pulse edge.}
    A \SI{50}{\milli\volt} step into \SI{200}{\nano\farad} is \SI{10}{\nano\coulomb}
    against a \(\sim\)\SI{2.2}{\micro\ampere} output stage, so the working
    electrode's virtual ground --- and with it the applied potential --- is
    wrong for \(\sim\)\SI{20}{\milli\second} after each edge. The settled
    samples are unaffected, but the transfer becomes superlinear above
    \(\sim\)\SI{350}{\nano\ampere} (up to \SI{30}{\percent} at the top of the
    tap; below that, proportional within \SI{3}{\percent}). The dose curves of
    Figure~\ref{fig:electrode-dose} therefore use a transfer \emph{measured}
    at eleven concentrations per reporter, not an assumed gain.
  \item \emph{Full scale is consumed by \(I(S_2)\), not \(\Delta I\).} The
    largest absolute sampled current is \(1.02\)--\(1.04\times\) the
    differential peak and reaches \SI{84}{\percent} of the
    \(\pm\SI{2.06}{\micro\ampere}\) tap for the largest reporter; headroom
    accounting must be done on \(I(S_2)\).
\end{itemize}
